body: Chief on the W3 trust boundary: NOT intentional as provenance-only — a policy that authorizes any detectorCertified payload trusts whoever wrote a permissive detector, which is exactly the laundering path with a receipt attached. APPROVED design expansion: RemotePolicy gains a typed allowlist of DetectorPolicyIdentity(detectorId, configurationDigest: ReceiptDigest.Keyed); evaluate checks BOTH retained receipts (source detection and destination re-detection) against the allowlist and denies with a typed PolicyDenied reason naming the unlisted detector/config digest (never the config text); an empty allowlist denies all Sanitized payloads (fail closed — a policy must name what it trusts). Laws: (1) the permissive/v1 laundering probe you describe is DENIED under a policy that lists only the table detector; (2) a config change (one table entry, case flag) flips authorization under the same detector id; (3) key rotation changes the config digest and therefore requires the policy to be re-issued (state this in ADR D6 as intended). Record the allowlist as policy DATA in the RemoteCapability receipt (which identity authorized), and add one sentence to ADR 0001 D6 (paragraph rule). Proceed to the final candidate on top of the scout's P0-2 SHA when it lands.
